全身正子攝影 [Clinical history] This 48-year-old male is a case of diffuse large B cell lymphoma, ABC-type, EBV-Negative, arising from follicular lymphoma, grade 3B. Blood sugar (on exam.): 90 mg/dl. [Procedure] Before the examination, the patient remained NPO except for water for about 6 hours. Serum glucose level was measured before administration of the radiotracer. The patient received 10 mCi of F-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) intravenously in the supine position and thereby stayed calm for one hour. Imaging acquisition was performed from head to feet by a PET/CT scanner (BIOGRAPH mCT Flow, Siemens, Germany) after voiding. The patient was placed in the scanner in the "arms-down" position. A CT acquisition was followed by a PET study. CT data were used for attenuation correction of PET. Transverse, coronal, and sagittal planes as well as a computerized cine mode PET image were reconstructed. [Findings] - s/p right neck lymph node excisional biopsy. Increased FDG uptake in the lymph nodes of the right neck (level I, SUV 3.59), left neck (level II, SUV 6.80), and left pterygoid (SUV 6.68). - Left neck level III-V lymph nodes are seen on CT images, with FDG uptake indistinguishable from the adjacent tissue. - Decreased FDG uptake in the bilateral cerebral regions, more prominent on the left side. - Increased FDG uptake in the left facet joint of L4-L5 (SUV 3.67). - The accumulation of FDG in the cerebral cortex, tonsils, myocardium, GI and GU tracts is considered to be physiological uptake. [Impression] 1. Suspect lymphoma involvement in the right neck level I, left neck level II, and left pterygoid lymph nodes. 2. Low metabolism in the left neck level III-V lymph nodes, possible reactive lymphadenopathy though lymphoma involvement cannot be completely excluded. 3. Compatible with encephalomalacia in the bilateral cerebral regions, more prominent on the left side. 4. Suspect arthritis in the left facet joint of L4-L5.

Delayed 4-hour images showed no redistribution in apex and anterior areas, partial redistribution in septum, inferoseptal and inferior areas, and decreased perufsion in anterolateral (medium size) area. [Impression] 1.Areas of non-viable myocardial tissue in the apex, and anterior (large size) wall. 2.Areas of mixed viable and non-viable myocardial tissues in the septum (large size), inferoseptal (large size) and inferior (large size) walls. 3.A medium area of reverse redistribution in the anterolateral wall. <Note> Reverse redistribution (RR) should be interpreted according to patient's condition: 1) In patients with known CAD but without previous MI, RR may be suggestive of multivessel disease. 2) In patients with chronic CAD and remote MI, RR is frequently associated with myocardial viability. 3) In patients with a low prevalence of CAD, the reality of RR is questionable. 4) In recent revascularized myocardial infarction, RR is associated with restoration of adequate perfusion and with myocardial salvage and viability.

[Clinical history] This 48-year-old male is a case of diffuse large B cell lymphoma, ABC-type, EBV-Negative, arising from follicular lymphoma, grade 3B. Blood sugar (on exam.): 90 mg/dl. [Procedure] Before the examination, the patient remained NPO except for water for about 6 hours. Serum glucose level was measured before administration of the radiotracer. The patient received 10 mCi of F-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) intravenously in the supine position and thereby stayed calm for one hour. Imaging acquisition was performed from head to feet by a PET/CT scanner (BIOGRAPH mCT Flow, Siemens, Germany) after voiding. The patient was placed in the scanner in the arms-down position. A CT acquisition was followed by a PET study. CT data were used for attenuation correction of PET. Transverse, coronal, and sagittal planes as well as a computerized cine mode PET image were reconstructed. [Findings] - s/p right neck lymph node excisional biopsy. Increased FDG uptake in the lymph nodes of the right neck (level I, SUV 3.59), left neck (level II, SUV 6.80), and left pterygoid (SUV 6.68). - Left neck level III-V lymph nodes are seen on CT images, with FDG uptake indistinguishable from the adjacent tissue. - Decreased FDG uptake in the bilateral cerebral regions, more prominent on the left side. - Increased FDG uptake in the left facet joint of L4-L5 (SUV 3.67). - The accumulation of FDG in the cerebral cortex, tonsils, myocardium, GI and GU tracts is considered to be physiological uptake. [Impression] 1. Suspect lymphoma involvement in the right neck level I, left neck level II, and left pterygoid lymph nodes. 2. Low metabolism in the left neck level III-V lymph nodes, possible reactive lymphadenopathy though lymphoma involvement cannot be completely excluded. 3. Compatible with encephalomalacia in the bilateral cerebral regions, more prominent on the left side. 4. Suspect arthritis in the left facet joint of L4-L5.

The stress images disclosed a small perfusion defect in the apical lateral area. Delayed 4-hour images showed complete redistribution in the apical lateral area and a small perfusion defect in the inferior wall. Imp: 1) A small area of ischemic myocardium tissue in the apical lateral wall. 2) A small area of reverse redistribution in the inferior wall. Note: Reverse redistribution (RR) should be interpreted according to patient's condition: 1) In patients with known CAD but without previous MI, RR may be suggestive of multivessel disease. 2) In patients with chronic CAD and remote MI, RR is frequently associated with myocardial viability. 3) In patients with a low prevalence of CAD, the reality of RR is questionable. 4) In recent revascularized myocardial infarction, RR is associated with restoration of adequate perfusion and with myocardial salvage and viability.
